text:
maya: FYI bringing up Mintaka-14B int4 in canary. Baseline perf looks fine for short chats but we're seeing intermittent OOMs and a quality dip on long summaries. Sharing initial observations.

devon: can you paste the canary config? Also which quant packing did you use for int4?

maya: used standard per-channel packing (pack-v1) + our new loose-alignment quant table. Canary config:
```
model: mintaka-14b-int4
batch_target: 16
max_new_tokens: 768
slot_compaction: enabled
slot_reserve: 0.05
prefetch: true
kv_trim_policy: auto
```

sophie: QA notes: long-form summaries (>400 tokens) have a jittery end-of-text behavior; we see ~3% ROUGE drop vs fp16 baseline and occasional abrupt truncation around 520-620 tokens.

ravi: infra profiler shows heavy allocation/deallocation spikes in the int4 allocator around the same time. That fits fragmentation -> OOM. Are the OOMs correlated with high batch concurrency or long max_new_tokens?

maya: so far it's mostly mixed traffic: lots of small chats plus some heavy long requests. The worst crash had batch concurrency 20 and several requests with max_new_tokens 1024.

devon: hypothesis: pack-v1 + slot_reserve 0.05 leaves small free slots scattered; with interleaved small/big requests allocation pattern fragments GPU heap. Also kv_trim_policy:auto might be triggering evictions mid-gen causing truncation.

sophie: can we reproduce with a synthetic mix? I can simulate a 70/30 short/long traffic pattern and run both pack-v1 and pack-v2 to compare.

maya: yes please. Proposed mitigations to test:
- lower batch_target to 8 for int4 canary
- cap hosted default max_new_tokens to 256 for Mintaka-int4 for now
- switch to pack-v2 packing (denser) and rerun quantized run
- temporarily set kv_trim_policy: conservative to avoid mid-gen evictions

ravi: infra action: enable eviction tracing and increase allocator sampling frequency for the canary namespace. I'll also pin runtime to rw-runtime v1.8.5-rc2 (has allocator metrics) on zone-2.

ci-bot: deploy-log: canary configs updated by maya at 2025-11-07T09:03:12Z -> batch_target=8, max_new_tokens=256, kv_trim_policy=conservative

devon: ran quick synthetic mix locally: pack-v2 reduces allocation peaks by ~22%, fewer small allocs observed. With batch=8 + max_new_tokens=256 I couldn't force an OOM in 30m load test.
sophie: QA sweep (100 long prompts) after pack-v2: ROUGE gap reduced to 0.6, truncation events dropped from 7 -> 1. Latency p50 ~+10% vs earlier, p95 unchanged.
maya: OK promising. Ravi, any red flags in allocator traces?
ravi: traces show fewer splits with pack-v2, but still see fragmentation when slot_compaction runs concurrently with prefetch. Filing INFRA-1252 to investigate compaction locking and prefetch allocation ordering.
maya: next steps:
- hold conservative defaults on hosted (batch 8 / max_new_tokens 256 / kv_trim_policy conservative)
- promote pack-v2 for Mintaka int4 quant artifacts and rerun full 200-prompt QA overnight
- infra to investigate slot_compaction vs prefetch interaction (INFRA-1252)
- revisit slot_reserve after allocator fixes

devon: I'll prepare a short playbook note for rollout: defaults + what to watch (eviction logs, profiler spikes, truncation counts).
sophie: posting full QA report in the morning thread.
maya: thanks team. If overnight run stays green we'll start a phased perf rollout next week and keep eviction tracing on for two weeks. :tada:
